opening:
The tavern had no king-seat.
Salmon Two-Arses found this offensive
until somebody explained
that every seat was built to survive him.

He climbed the strongest table,
tested it with one short leg,
raised the first of twelve pints,
and called for lies to leave by the nearest door.

No polished heroes tonight.
No dead made useful.
No lovers melted into one obedient shape.
No daughter sung as somebody else's half.
No wound turned golden
because a bard lacked courage to name blood.

We sing the whole ones:
frightened and furious,
wrong and returning,
living, dead, dog, warrior,
wife beside husband,
sister beside sister,
beloved beside beloved,
never beneath.

Fill ten cups.
Leave an eleventh place open
for the listener who needs the road.

When I call a name,
answer not with worship.
Answer:
We know you were here.

And if I fall from this table,
let the record show
the floor attacked first.

odes.title: FATAS AND THE THUNDER TAUGHT MERCY
odes.dedication: For the boy before the Raven, the man beneath the name, and the hand that made an axe answerable.
odes.bard: Raised by Salmon Two-Arses after ordering the room to put every weapon where its owner could still refuse it.
odes.refrain: LAY THE THUNDER DOWN. LET THE LIVING CHOOSE.
body:
Before the road named him Raven,
there was a boy who learned doors badly:
doors that listened,
doors that kept,
doors whose hinges knew the weight of fear
better than the hands that opened them.

He grew with a storm behind the ribs,
and when Skuldrend came into his keeping,
the old iron found a man already fluent
in the language of breaking.
That is where lesser songs begin boasting.
This one begins with the binding cloth.

For he wrapped the edge.
He carried thunder across hunger-roads,
past white coats and red ledgers,
past water taught obedience
and villages fined for kindness.
Again and again the world offered him
the clean red answer.
Again and again he made the answer wait.

At the sheepfold, children watched.
At the dry bend, Maisie burned with anger.
At the counted road, a whole system leaned close,
hoping the wounded man would become
the violent proof already written for him.
FATAS swallowed iron
and kept the axe upon his back.

Do not call that gentleness.
Gentleness was never the bargain.
Call it mastery hard enough
to leave bruises upon the soul.
Call it rage made answerable.
Call it the Raven refusing
to feed the cage with his own legend.

When the roots beneath law rose hungry,
Skuldrend learned a better cut:
not flesh,
not grief,
not the frightened hand tangled in command,
but claim,
commission,
ownership,
the sentence that said another life belonged.

Kingship came dressed as gratitude.
Keeper came dressed as need.
Source came dressed as destiny.
Every throne whispered the same lie:
Only you can hold us together.
FATAS answered with the oldest road-law:
Then learn to stand without kneeling to me.

Ness stood beside him,
not behind,
not beneath,
not captured by the word wife.
Her thumb found his pulse
when false peace wore her face.
He knew the imitation by its kindness:
it told him he had done enough.
The true Ness would have told him to wash first.
He laughed, and the lie lost its doorway.

So remember him whole:
not only Raven,
not only axe-bearer,
not only the man who walks first into darkness,
but the boy who still feels old houses close,
the husband who accepts a hand at his pulse,
the leader who leaves standing-room for others,
the furious man who asks witness before force.

Many carried sharper blades.
Many made taller speeches.
But when the roads, roots, Crowns and Houses
tried to turn one wounded life into a throne,
FATAS did the greater thing.
He remained a man.

Raise no crown above him.
Set no law beyond reply.
Wrap the edge until the hour is true.
And if the hour becomes true,
cut the chain,
not the chained.
LAY THE THUNDER DOWN. LET THE LIVING CHOOSE.

odes.title: NESS AND THE LAW THAT ATE BREAD
odes.dedication: For Crow, terms-maker, wife without ownership, and the woman who could make a room confess.
odes.bard: Remembered by Salmon Two-Arses, who insisted this ode be served with bread before anybody was permitted an opinion.
odes.refrain: BREAD FIRST. BREATH FIRST. LET LOVE KEEP ITS EARS.
body:
Ness never mistook noise for danger
or silence for peace.
While warriors watched the doorway,
she watched the room:
who had gone pale,
who had stopped speaking,
who held a cup too tightly,
who was being thanked into a debt.

That was how Crow saw the snare.
Not when iron closed.
Earlier.
When kindness changed its voice.
When a bowl began counting gratitude.
When a healer decided calm mattered
more than the self left breathing beneath it.

The Count offered order.
The Duchess offered private mercy.
The Agreement offered rest without friction.
Ness heard the hook under every soft word.
She did not answer with a softer lie.
She answered with terms.

Food creates no debt.
Shelter owns no guest.
Care does not become custody by morning.
No law before food.
No testimony taken from hunger.
No frightened yes polished into forever.

There are axe-songs for cutting gates.
There should be more songs
for the woman who keeps a spoon
from becoming a sceptre.

At Witness Isle she did not build a court.
She built a habit:
ask again,
name the present choice,
leave the visible exits open,
let anger speak without crowning it,
let grief remain untidy enough to be true.

Beside FATAS she carried no leash.
She did not cure the boy beneath Raven.
She did not save him into owing her.
She stood near enough for return
and far enough for choice.
That distance was their marriage-road.

Once, memory brought her sister near.
The old lesson came by a cup-handle:
hear the want first, Ness.
The Ledger tried to call it selfishness.
Crow corrected the wood.
Self among others.
Not before.
Not erased beneath.

Then came the sentence
worth carving above every tavern door:
Love has ears.

Not hands that seize before asking.
Not eyes that watch until watch becomes cage.
Ears.
Love listens long enough
for the beloved to remain inconvenient.

At the abyss she stood over a mouth
that promised painless joining.
It had swallowed grief
and called the silence mercy.
Ness named the theft.
Pain is not your property.
Captivity is not comfort.
Love reaches across darkness;
it does not erase the space between.

The dead heard her.
The drowned heard her.
The living, exhausted and quarrelsome,
heard themselves return.

So if Crow enters your hall,
hide no debt in the welcome.
Put the board low.
Leave the door honest.
Feed the child before asking the child
to explain the world.

And if a law objects,
give the law bread.
Make it chew slowly.
Then ask whether it has finally learned
that a full mouth is not permission to speak for another.
BREAD FIRST. BREATH FIRST. LET LOVE KEEP ITS EARS.

odes.title: MIA AND THE GATE THAT FAILED TO DIVIDE HER
odes.dedication: For the fast hand, the returning daughter, and the woman who learned that protection must still ask.
odes.bard: Set to the table by Salmon Two-Arses, who claimed every gate has two weaknesses: truth and somebody too stubborn to queue.
odes.refrain: NOT HALF. NOT KEY. NOT YOURS TO DIVIDE.
body:
Mia learned early that systems love daughters
when daughters can be made into doors.
A bloodline for the lock.
A body for the hinge.
A name that explains another name.
A life reduced to what it opens.

The Crown took her into clean marble,
where every wall pretended
that captivity became mercy
if the floor was swept.
Yet the Spirit-March found her.
Far from low tide,
salt woke upon her tongue.
Kian held the seam.
Bella burned blue.
The perfect record took a stain.

Mia returned carrying speed like a blade.
She moved first,
decided quickly,
found the body that needed lifting
while older minds still named the problem.
It saved lives.
It also taught her the hardest wound:
protection can become a thief
when love chooses for the loved.

Myah stood beside that lesson.
Not prize.
Not patient.
Not the quiet life Mia must manage.
When false Mara wore the face of longing,
Mia did not purchase comfort
with Myah's separate will.
Together they remembered the missing sister
with faults sharp enough to break the saint-mask:
bad whistle,
boiled eel hated,
a priest once punched.
Ordinary truth defeated holy bait.

At the tables of Witness Isle,
Mia became the hand that wrote precisely:
loss happened.
Some trace washed away.
Some trace was lifted.
Both true.

That was her new swiftness:
not racing past pain,
but catching the lie
before it dressed pain as blame.

Then the Ledger turned upon the sisters.
One story, it wrote.
One mother.
One divided sign.

Mia looked at Maisie.
Maisie looked back.
Between them stood every power
that had tried to make twins convenient.

Not one story, Mia wrote.
Two stories braided.

The wood tried again:
Mother would want.

No.
The dead mother would not become a puppet.
Her name was not a net.
It was a door before which two daughters
could stand differently and remain daughters still.

Mia's mark curved inward that day,
question guarding a candle.
Do not call the shape permanent.
She never belonged to a symbol long enough
for symbols to own her.

Call her fighter.
Call her healer of the immediate hour.
Call her keeper of ugly accuracy.
Call her beloved, sister, daughter, mother
only where the living meaning allows.

But when the old gate asks
which half has returned,
answer with the name that survived it:
Mia.

Whole when frightened.
Whole when wrong.
Whole when learning to ask.
Whole when her quick hand opens
and lets another hand choose
whether to meet it.
NOT HALF. NOT KEY. NOT YOURS TO DIVIDE.

odes.title: MAISIE AND THE SECOND STORY
odes.dedication: For the hand that lowered the stone, the blood that learned to answer, and the sister who would not be edited into half a life.
odes.bard: Sung by Salmon Two-Arses with a river-stone upon the table and strict instructions that nobody throw it until the rhyme had improved.
odes.refrain: TWO DAUGHTERS. TWO ROADS. LET NEITHER BECOME THE OTHER.
body:
At the watched road, Maisie found a stone
that fitted fury like a promise.
The counted carts passed.
The white authority watched.
Every insult in the world became a window
and invited her arm through.
She raised it.

There are songs that would end the verse there,
stone flying,
glass breaking,
anger made simple enough for applause.
But Maisie saw the trap before release:
the waiting record,
the charge already inked,
the hungry machine needing one small violence
to call all resistance savage.
She set the stone down.

Do not mistake this for surrender.
The stone remembered the heat of her palm.
So did she.
Restraint did not cancel anger.
It kept anger hers.

Later, on ground that listened too closely,
her shin opened against the world.
Blood touched earth.
Roots shifted below the roots.
Something old heard a name in pain
and leaned upward.

Maisie did not hide behind accident.
She said she had made it worse.
FATAS answered with the mercy of precision:
Yes.
And you stopped.
That matters.

So she learned the anchor-lines:
not chains,
not orders disguised as ropes,
but ways for the willing to find one another
when mist taught distance to lie.
Scarlet came bright through the dark,
not mount, not emblem, not possession,
but living answer beside living answer.

James came carrying suffering
and the hope that suffering might excuse him.
Maisie did not deny the wound.
Neither did she let the wound become a key
to every locked consequence.
Pain may explain the theft.
It does not return the stolen choice.
Forgiveness, if it comes,
comes walking,
not summoned by the thief's tears.

Then the Ledger found the twins.
It sharpened its neatest knife
and called the blade unity.

One mother, it wrote.
One wound.
One story divided into two useful bodies.

Maisie looked upon Mia
and saw no mirror.
She saw the sister who moved first,
the fighter whose love sometimes outran permission,
the woman whose history touched hers
without consuming it.

Mia looked back
and saw the hand that had lowered the stone,
the keeper of lines,
the fury that could stop itself
without becoming tame.

Not one story, they answered.
Two stories braided.

The watching power sneered:
You have never seen hair.

It understood nothing.
A braid is not sameness.
It is difference held close
without either strand disappearing.

That is Maisie's endurance:
not purity,
not the false heroism of never being wrong,
but the brave second motion.
The arm raised—then lowered.
The blood spilled—then answered for.
The bond wounded—then judged without haste.
The story offered as half—then taken back whole.

Put no halo on her anger.
Put no muzzle on it either.
Give her the stone.
Give her the open ground.
Trust her to know the difference
between a weapon and a witness.

Maisie.
The second story.
Not the lesser one.
TWO DAUGHTERS. TWO ROADS. LET NEITHER BECOME THE OTHER.

odes.title: MYAH AND THE VOICE BENEATH THE VOW
odes.dedication: For the fen-born listener, the daughter no House could replace, and the silence that remained a living position.
odes.bard: Given by Salmon Two-Arses after he requested one minute of quiet, survived nine heartbeats of it, and accused the rafters of heckling.
odes.refrain: SILENCE IS STANDING. WAIT FOR THE CHOSEN SOUND.
body:
Myah came from water that remembers footsteps,
from reed-country where a path may be true at dawn
and drowned by noon,
from old vows flowering under old grief.

Blómblaða called her daughter,
and the word carried roots.
Not every root is a shackle.
Not every blossom is kind.
She learned to hear the difference
before others knew there was a sound.

Mara was missing.
Absence sat at every meal
and learned the shape of the family.
So when the dark offered Mara back,
it chose the beloved face,
the remembered cadence,
the ache most willing to believe.

But the false sister remembered being loved
and could not remember loving.
She knew the shelter given to her,
not the shelter she had given.
She wore sainthood too smoothly.

Myah and Mia answered with mortal details:
a bad whistle,
boiled eel hated,
a priest once struck,
the glorious small faults
by which the loved remain people.
The holy mask cracked.
The fragments below did not vanish.
Neither did longing become consent.

There had been a collar.
There had been a knot.
There had been hands that called ownership
protection, medicine, destiny, need.
When the fastening broke,
the world expected a speech.

Myah gave it breath.
Then a tap.
Then thread drawn once between fingers.
Then, when the word was hers,
the word.

No bard may hurry this part.
No healer may count quiet as absence.
No lover may translate stillness into yes.
Silence is not an empty chair.
It is someone sitting there.
The House wrote upon its hungry threshold:

Daughter required.
May replace.

Mia would have entered for her.
Love surged forward, armed and immediate.
Myah stopped it.
She would not be saved by becoming debt.
She would not allow Mia to become substitute flesh.
And she would not let the House define daughter
as a space any grieving woman might fill.
No replacement, she answered.
The doors disliked grammar after that.

Across road, fen, Ledger and listening dark,
Myah kept the decision-layer alive:
What is asked?
Who is answering?
Can the answer change?
Where is the exit?

Simple questions.
King-killers.

Her forgiveness was never a public feast.
It was measured in chosen nearness,
in the right to stop,
in the right not to explain the stopping.
Some wounds closed like doors.
Some stayed open to weather.
Neither condition made her unfinished.

So do not praise her merely for surviving silence.
Praise the precision with which she made silence speak.
Praise the listener who forced mighty rooms to wait.
Praise the daughter who loved roots
and still refused their claim upon her body.

When she taps once, attend.
When she draws the thread, do not seize it.
When she names herself, do not complete the sentence.

The fen has three skies.
Myah needs only one voice.
Her own.
SILENCE IS STANDING. WAIT FOR THE CHOSEN SOUND.

odes.title: LUCY BLADE-WIT AND THE LIVING FIRST
odes.dedication: For the healer with an edge, the beloved who argued honestly, and the woman who kept symbols from killing their subjects.
odes.bard: Roared by Salmon Two-Arses, who submitted himself for medical examination and was diagnosed as "mostly tavern, with complications."
odes.refrain: LIVING BODIES FIRST. LET THE GRAND WORDS LIMP BEHIND.
body:
Lucy was named Blade-Wit
because language sharpened when she held it.
She could pare a pompous oath
down to the frightened wish inside.
She could make a war council remember
that bleeding is not metaphor.

Where others saw vessels,
thresholds,
keys,
chosen blood,
ancestral doors,
Lucy saw a person with cold fingers
who needed broth,
stitches,
space,
and the truth before treatment.
Living bodies first.

It sounded small beside prophecy.
That was why prophecy feared it.

She learned every soft danger:
rest that erased,
calm that overruled,
care that kept no doorway open,
medicine administered to make a room convenient.
Hearth-Soothe could lower terror.
It could also lower refusal.
Lucy made the distinction stand upright
even when everyone was tired.
Especially when everyone was tired.

Jesse loved plans.
Lucy loved Jesse.
These were not always peaceful facts.
He saw a failing line
and wanted every body placed for survival.
She saw the same line
and heard an old command hiding
inside the word protection.
They argued.

Not the pretty quarrel of a minstrel's courtship,
resolved by rain and kissing.
They struck the iron point:
Can love restrain the beloved for safety?
Who decides when the danger is real?
What if the protector is exhausted?
What if the refusal is frightened?

The Hollow wanted one answer.
Their honesty broke it into human pieces.

At Greyfen, when the world leaned symbolic,
when every path wished to become sacrifice,
Lucy seized Jesse with both hands
and gave him the blessing no grand temple knew:
Do not die in the symbolic direction.

It was funny.
It was furious.
It was a rope thrown across the abyss.

He chose her aloud.
Not as cure.
Not as reward.
As the person before him,
difficult and breathing,
whose connection required effort.
Lucy asked no better love than effort awake.

She endured because she never allowed endurance
to become a demand made upon the wounded.
She bandaged what could be bandaged.
She cursed what deserved cursing.
She knew laughter sometimes returns the border
between a person and the terror consuming the room.

When councils grew solemn enough to murder,
her wit opened a window.
When myth called pain necessary,
she asked whose pain.
When destiny called a body temporary,
she planted both boots and made destiny repeat itself.

Call her sharp.
Call her angry.
Call her the hand that checks the pulse
while heroes debate the soul.
Call her beloved without making her gentle.

Her victory was never spotless survival.
It was this:
after Crown, Hollow, road and root,
after every noble phrase tried to spend her,
Lucy remained—by her own preferred miracle—
irritatingly alive.
LIVING BODIES FIRST. LET THE GRAND WORDS LIMP BEHIND.

odes.title: JESSE AND THE LINE THAT SHOOK
odes.dedication: For the planner who heard command inside his own care, the brother called Jay by the dead, and the man who learned that steadiness is not stillness.
odes.bard: Counted out by Salmon Two-Arses with six cups, four spoons, a salt-cellar and one pickled onion representing forces of uncertain loyalty.
odes.refrain: A LINE MAY SHAKE AND STILL BE CHOSEN.
body:
Jesse knew the price of badly placed feet.
He saw paths before others saw ground:
where a crowd would narrow,
where a bridge would lie,
where fear would turn a doorway
into teeth.

Old debt had taught him.
Contract-metal had remembered him.
Harl Venn's shadow did not need a body
to keep a clause alive.
So Jesse learned contingencies,
counts,
the mercy of a second route.

Useful knowledge.
Dangerous comfort.

For the planner begins by moving markers,
and one tired night may forget
that every marker has a mouth.

He did not forget cleanly.
No worthy person does.
Fatigue entered his care
and dressed itself as necessity.
The enemy's oldest logic came out
in Jesse's own responsible voice:
hold them now,
explain later,
keep them safe until they understand.

Lucy heard it.
Worse—Jesse heard it after she answered.

There stands the measure of him:
not that control never tempted,
but that he let the accusation land.
He did not build intention into a fortress.
He did not say love made the harm impossible.
He opened the plan to witness.

Check me, then.
Ask again.
Tell me when the line I hold
has become a leash.

The listening road chose a crueller weapon.
It borrowed his dead brother's voice.
It used the name kept for old closeness:
Jay.

One syllable,
and every map inside him folded.

Come this way, said the beloved dead.
There is rest beyond the next turning.
There is a version of duty
in which nobody can be lost again.

But grief that knows a private name
is not therefore truth.
Jesse stood upon the shaking line
and tested what the voice required.
It required surrender without return.
It required him alone.
It made memory into an order.

He refused the order
without refusing the brother.
That is a grief-feat no axe can perform.

At Greyfen the line failed honestly.
Earth shifted.
Signals broke.
Every clean formation became people
calling through bad air.
Lucy was there—sharp, frightened, alive—
and Jesse chose her publicly.

Not above the others.
Not as the reason others mattered less.
He chose the connection itself:
the difficult bridge maintained from both ends,
the beloved who could contradict him
and remain beloved.

Later he put his shoulder to a wooden lever.
No legendary blade.
No ancestral title.
A practical length of timber,
splintered where hands had used it.

That suited him.
Jesse's best work was never the shining plan.
It was the revision made when a living voice said no.
It was the route redrawn around the injured.
It was the hand staying on the lever
while the elegant answer broke.

Sing him without polishing the fault away.
Sing the contract scars.
Sing Jay across the false road.
Sing Lucy's anger and his listening.
Sing the tactician who learned
that trust is not the absence of checks,
but the courage to remain checkable.

The line shook because Jesse was mortal.
The line held because he did not pretend otherwise.
A LINE MAY SHAKE AND STILL BE CHOSEN.

odes.title: ELDWYN AND THE ROOTS THAT LOST THE ARGUMENT
odes.dedication: For Elland's pupil, keeper of the imperfect draught, and the scholar who would enter the world's wound carrying questions instead of ownership.
odes.bard: Recited by Salmon Two-Arses after tasting Hearth-Soothe without permission and reporting that it possessed "an unnecessarily judgmental finish." The cup was removed from him.
odes.refrain: CALM IS NOT QUIET. KNOWLEDGE IS NOT COMMAND.
body:
Elland did not leave Eldwyn certainty.
He left fragments,
soot-notes,
failed measures,
warnings crowded into margins,
the long humility of a medicine
that had harmed before it healed.

Hearth-Soothe was not born perfect.
It was argued into mercy.
Too much, and fear vanished
with the person who needed to name it.
Too little, and terror kept the whole room.
Every dose asked an ethical question
no bottle could answer alone.

When the shaking boy came,
others counted coats,
slates,
symptoms,
possible trouble.
Eldwyn knelt and raised his hand.
Count my fingers.

Not the guards.
Not the marks against you.
Not what the room has already decided.
Here.
Now.
My fingers.

Only after the boy returned to himself
did Eldwyn offer the smallest help.
Offer—not verdict.

That was his scholarship:
knowledge forced to knock.

He read Root,
Watcher,
Door,
Hidden,
Blood,
Choice.
The old signs formed patterns under his gaze,
but he would not call a pattern innocent
merely because it was ancient.

Maps wanted worship.
Runes wanted completion.
Dead masters wanted their students
to mistake inheritance for obedience.
Eldwyn kept asking the impolite question:
What did this do to the living?

The Hollow shaped Ulrike for him,
thinking affection was easily copied.
It built the remembered face,
the known voice,
the version without inconvenient refusal.

Eldwyn looked at the smooth counterfeit
and almost pitied it.
The real Ulrike was irreducible,
furious in directions no trap could schedule.
Good luck with her, he told the dark.

Somewhere beyond imitation,
a true pulse answered.
He did not declare her saved.
He declared the search unfinished.

Jórunn walked beside his work
with a discipline not swallowed by his own.
Two practices met there,
sometimes agreeing,
sometimes sharpening each other's borders.
Closeness did not confer expertise.
Love did not erase method.

Then came the white leaf,
impossible and inviting,
the sort of object from which disasters hatch
when scholars say destiny.

Eldwyn called himself academically curious.
Jórunn heard the danger contained
in those two innocent words.
So did everyone else.

Laugh—but keep the lantern lit.
Curiosity was his wound and instrument.
He followed roots where roots went wrong,
not because darkness made him chosen,
but because somebody had to record
where wonder became appetite.

He endured Elland without becoming Elland.
He carried the draught without calling it cure.
He studied the old powers
without offering them the compliment of awe.

The world is worse than the first map says.
Eldwyn knows.
His oath is not to deny it.
His oath is to refuse to leave it there.

So fill the scholar's cup only halfway.
Leave room for revision.
Mark every bottle.
Keep the exits visible.
And when the deep roots claim
that what is known must therefore be obeyed,
send Eldwyn down with lamp, question,
and the unbearable patience to prove them wrong.
CALM IS NOT QUIET. KNOWLEDGE IS NOT COMMAND.

odes.title: KIAN AND THE TWO AXES BEYOND THE FIRE
odes.dedication: For the defender of Greystone, the dead man who did not counterfeit return, and the duty that crossed the mist without claiming life again.
odes.bard: Hammered out by Salmon Two-Arses with two wood-axes laid flat before him. Their owner watched closely. So did the table.
odes.refrain: TWO AXES AT THE MIST-LINE. ONE DUTY DEATH COULD NOT OWN.
body:
When the Crown came to Greystone,
it brought soldiers,
nets,
banners,
and the great official confidence
of men who think a village is conquered
once its doors have been counted.
Kian stood where counting became difficult.

He was not made from prophecy.
He was made from the useful angers:
the gate barred in time,
the warning given plainly,
the neighbour not abandoned
because the odds had acquired uniforms.

Two axes became his grammar.
No flourish.
No courtly steel.
Work-blades answering work that had turned murderous.

He endured the raids,
the crossings,
the long narrowing of safe ground.
He stood with Edwill,
with the dogs,
with Bella moving where trust moved,
while the tide drew the world tight.

At the low-tide choke,
death ceased circling and entered him.
Say it without mist.
Kian died at low tide.

The axes fell quiet.
Bella laid her head upon his chest.
No song made the chest rise.
No love, however faithful,
was ordered to pretend.

They built the pyre.
Flame opened what grief could not:
the Spirit-March,
reed-gold beyond smoke,
the honoured dead held not as prisoners
but as those who had chosen one last boundary.
Kian rose there.

Do not say returned.
He did not wake hungry.
He did not sit to breakfast.
He did not cancel the wound in those who burned him.
Death remained true.
So did Kian.

Reed-gold at the mist-line,
two axes bright in hands beyond flesh,
he entered the later struggle
under terms the living did not own.

At the Sentinel's ritual heart,
both blades answered.
Old machinery learned
that the dead need not serve the power
that understands only possession.

He brought warning as well as force:
roots below roots were gathering,
the deep dark teaching itself new hunger.
Kian did not claim to know the whole design.
He carried what he had seen
to those who could still choose what followed.

This is how he endured through the books:
not preserved,
not restored,
not made into an immortal convenience,
but bounded.

He could appear where vow and road permitted.
He could fight where the old passage opened.
He could not be owned by longing.
He could not be summoned to soothe every grief.

Honour the limit.
The limit is what keeps love from lying.

When the mist shines reed-gold,
when two axe-heads catch a fire
no living forge has made,
raise the cup—but leave the empty place empty.

Kian stands there because he died.
Kian stands there because duty survived him.
Both truths hold.
Neither kneels.
TWO AXES AT THE MIST-LINE. ONE DUTY DEATH COULD NOT OWN.

odes.title: BELLA AND THE BLUE FLAME THAT CAME HOME
odes.dedication: For the hound before the omen, the witness beside the dead, and the blue fire that never forgot it had once been warm.
odes.bard: Offered by Salmon Two-Arses after every dog in the tavern received meat, every human was searched for hidden meat, and the bard was found guilty on seven counts.
odes.refrain: BLUE AT THE HEARTH. LOVE REMAINS; DEATH REMAINS TOO.
body:
Before the blue flame,
Bella was a dog.
Begin there.

Warm flank.
Salt in the coat.
Nose reading news from the wind.
Ears lifting before the watchman heard.
The patient weight beside a boot
that told a tired fighter
he had not yet become alone.

She did not need to symbolize loyalty.
She practised it.
She did not represent love.
She chose where to lie down.

At the low-tide choke,
Kian's heart stopped beneath the ruin.
Bella placed her head upon his chest
and kept the first honest watch.

Not waiting for movement.
Not bargaining.
Knowing.

When the pyre took him,
the March opened reed-gold,
and beside that gold moved blue-white fire:
Bella beyond flesh,
still herself,
death neither erased nor made master.

Together does not mean the same.
She was not Kian's shadow.
She was not an ornament on his afterlife.
Blue beside gold.
Witness beside warrior.
Each name carrying its own boundary.

In the orchard, corrupted roots recoiled.
Not because Bella had become a weapon,
but because certain hungers cannot bear
a presence that remembers love
without converting it into ownership.

At the hearth where terms were spoken,
her flame became a sterner law than ink.
When words kept choice open,
blue warmed.
When a smooth phrase hid coercion,
the light thinned,
sank cold,
and every liar discovered
that a dog may cross death
without learning diplomacy.

Sometimes her meaning travelled through Jorn.
Do not confuse the road with the traveller.
Bella did not become Jorn.
Jorn did not become Bella.
One voice may carry another's warning
and still belong to its own mouth.

Later, another dog might answer
to the same beloved name.
Names travel.
Affection repeats its music.
That is not proof a body has returned.
The new living deserve their own life;
the dead deserve the dignity of having died.
Bella keeps both dignities.

She endures not as a pet preserved in amber,
nor as a convenient miracle at every door.
She comes where witness matters:
where grief is being rewritten,
where a vow grows slippery,
where power hopes nobody will smell
the old blood under fresh language.
Then blue gathers by the hearth.

The grand speakers pause.
The frightened breathe.
Somewhere in the light remains
the dog who once leaned warm against a leg,
who knew Kian living,
who knew him dead,
and loved him without falsifying either state.

No crown fits her.
No leash reaches her.
Give her no human sermon.
Give her meat when she is flesh,
truth when she is flame,
and room beside the one she chose.

The last cup stands upon the floor.
The blue light touches it.
Nobody commands her to drink.
BLUE AT THE HEARTH. LOVE REMAINS; DEATH REMAINS TOO.

closing:
The room held ten names
and did not close around them.

FATAS—thunder laid down.
Ness—bread before judgment.
Mia—not half.
Maisie—the second story.
Myah—the chosen sound.
Lucy—the living first.
Jesse—the shaking line.
Eldwyn—the unanswered question.
Kian—two axes beyond fire.
Bella—blue at the hearth.

Salmon Two-Arses raised the eleventh cup,
the one left open for the listener.

"If you found yourself in none of them," he said,
"drink because the road has farther to go.
If you found yourself in all of them,
drink water and seek professional counsel."

The hall laughed,
which is one way a hall keeps breathing.

Then every hand struck table once.
Not worship.
Witness.

The rafters returned it.
The floor returned it.
Far below, the oldest roots
found no command inside the words
and therefore could not swallow them.

Salmon drank the twelfth pint,
began the perilous three-yard pilgrimage
to the karsi,
and was discovered three days later
upon the throne,
stuck fast to the seat
but still correcting the rhyme.

Outside, dawn entered Vardrum
without banner or permission.
The road beyond the tavern waited.
